\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ہنسانا} (hãsānā)}{ہنسانا (hãsānā)}]{\ur{ہنسانا} (hãsānā) — to make (someone) laugh}

\label{lesson:UR-C453-hasana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for fussiness, then the Urdu for haughtiness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ہنسانا}}
\textbf{\ur{ہنسانا}} — \emph{hãsānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to make (someone) laugh\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میرا} \ur{بھائی} \ur{سب} \ur{کو} \ur{ہنساتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{merā bhāī sab ko hãsātā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother makes everyone laugh.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچوں} \ur{کو} \ur{ہنسایا}, \emph{us ne bachchoṅ ko hãsāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ہنسانا}} (\emph{hãsānā}) is the causative of \textbf{\ur{ہنسنا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to laugh\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Sanskrit \emph{hásati}, \textquotedblleft{}laughs\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 14021).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hãsānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hãsānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{merā bhāī sab ko hãsātā hai.} — My brother makes everyone laugh.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for fussiness, then the Urdu for haughtiness, then say \emph{hãsānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ہنسانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To make (someone) laugh\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رلانا} (rulānā)}{رلانا (rulānā)}]{\ur{رلانا} (rulānā) — to make (someone) cry}

\label{lesson:UR-C453-rulana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for haughtiness, then the Urdu for to make (someone) laugh.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رلانا}}
\textbf{\ur{رلانا}} — \emph{rulānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to make (someone) cry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{فلم} \ur{نے} \ur{سب} \ur{کو} \ur{رلایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{is film ne sab ko rulāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This film made everyone cry.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بہن} \ur{کو} \ur{رلایا}, \emph{us ne bahan ko rulāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رلانا}} (\emph{rulānā}) is the causative of \textbf{\ur{رونا}}, \textquotedblleft{}to cry\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Sanskrit \emph{rōdati}, \textquotedblleft{}howls, weeps\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10840).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rulānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rulānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{is film ne sab ko rulāyā.} — This film made everyone cry.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for haughtiness, then the Urdu for to make (someone) laugh, then say \emph{rulānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{رلانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To make (someone) cry\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{قہقہہ} (qahqahā)}{قہقہہ (qahqahā)}]{\ur{قہقہہ} (qahqahā) — a burst of laughter}

\label{lesson:UR-C453-qahqaha}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to make (someone) laugh, then the Urdu for to make (someone) cry.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{قہقہہ}}
\textbf{\ur{قہقہہ}} — \emph{qahqahā} — \textquotedblleft{}a burst of laughter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{مجھے} \ur{اس} \ur{کا} \ur{قہقہہ} \ur{بہت} \ur{اچھا} \ur{لگتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mujhe us kā qahqahā bahut achchhā lagtā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I really like her loud laugh.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{قہقہہ}} (\emph{qahqahā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{qahqaha}, \textquotedblleft{}loud laughter\textquotedblright{}, a word that imitates the sound.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qahqahā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{qahqahā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mujhe us kā qahqahā bahut achchhā lagtā hai.} — I really like her loud laugh.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to make (someone) laugh, then the Urdu for to make (someone) cry, then say \emph{qahqahā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سسکنا} (sisaknā)}{سسکنا (sisaknā)}]{\ur{سسکنا} (sisaknā) — to sob}

\label{lesson:UR-C453-sisakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to make (someone) cry, then the Urdu for a burst of laughter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سسکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سسکنا}} — \emph{sisaknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to sob\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{لڑکی} \ur{کونے} \ur{میں} \ur{بیٹھ} \ur{کر} \ur{سسک} \ur{رہی} \ur{تھی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{laṛkī kone meṅ baiṭh kar sisak rahī thī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The girl was sitting in the corner, sobbing.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{دیر} \ur{تک} \ur{سسکی}, \emph{voh der tak siskī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سسکنا}} (\emph{sisaknā}) is probably inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi \emph{siskārī}, \textquotedblleft{}sobbing\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{śuṣati}, \textquotedblleft{}hisses, pants\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 12545).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sisaknā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sisaknā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{laṛkī kone meṅ baiṭh kar sisak rahī thī.} — The girl was sitting in the corner, sobbing.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to make (someone) cry, then the Urdu for a burst of laughter, then say \emph{sisaknā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{سسکنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To sob\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مذاق} (mazāq)}{مذاق (mazāq)}]{\ur{مذاق} (mazāq) — teasing; fun}

\label{lesson:UR-C453-mazaq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a burst of laughter, then the Urdu for to sob.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مذاق}}
\textbf{\ur{مذاق}} — \emph{mazāq} — \textquotedblleft{}teasing; fun\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{میں} \ur{نے} \ur{یہ} \ur{بات} \ur{مذاق} \ur{میں} \ur{کہی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{maiṅ ne yih bāt mazāq meṅ kahī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I said it in fun.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مذاق}} (\emph{mazāq}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{madhāq}, \textquotedblleft{}taste\textquotedblright{}; the sense \textquotedblleft{}fun, teasing\textquotedblright{} is the one Urdu gives it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mazāq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{maiṅ ne yih bāt mazāq meṅ kahī.} — I said it in fun.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a burst of laughter, then the Urdu for to sob, then say \emph{mazāq} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
